The second edition of the World Humanoid Robot Games kicked off in China on Saturday.

The competition will run for five days and has already included a robot running faster than Usain Bolt's 100m sprint world record.

Elsewhere at the event in Beijing, a robot performed Cristiano Ronaldo's iconic 'Siuuu' celebration on the football pitch and droids took part in synchronised marching at its opening ceremony.

Robots have also been competing in events including boxing, high jump and table tennis.

title.en: Zelensky has 'questions to answer' about corruption in his government, sacked minister tells BBC
title.zh: 被解职部长告诉BBC：泽连斯基政府内部腐败“有待解答”

summary.en: Ukraine's former defense minister, recently dismissed from his post, has publicly stated that President Zelensky faces significant questions regarding corruption within his administration. The former minister also advocated for new elections to be held in the country.
summary.zh: 乌克兰前国防部长在被解职后公开表示，泽连斯基总统需要回答有关其政府内部腐败的问题。这位前部长还呼吁在乌克兰举行新的选举。

body.en:
Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky has "questions to answer" about corruption in his government, his sacked defence minister Mykhailo Fedorov has told the BBC.

Fedorov, a popular minister who modernised the armed forces and pioneered drone warfare, was fired last month after reportedly falling out with the head of Ukraine's armed forces.

He told the BBC a money laundering investigation announced last week raised questions about Zelensky's awareness of potential corruption in his inner circle.

Fedorov also reiterated that "democracy should not be the hostage of Putin" - but stopped short of declaring his own political ambitions days after he posted a video calling for elections in Ukraine.

There were angry protests over his sacking but his support dwindled and demonstrations ended on Wednesday, after Fedorov's replacement was confirmed. His call for a wartime vote has been largely rejected.

Asked whether he missed his old job, the 35-year-old replied "No", citing the relentless stress of managing Ukraine's war with Russia while transforming its defence ministry.

Ukraine has been under martial law since Russia's full-scale invasion in 2022, meaning elections are suspended.

But Fedorov said it was his "moral right" to start the conversation about elections.

"We should not be afraid of discussing it. That's what democracy is all about. If I cannot share my ideas and be open about them with my own society, then what are we fighting for?"

In his earlier video statement Fedorov had argued that "people cannot endlessly live in a state where they do not understand why certain decisions are made".

He shied away from criticising the president directly and declined to answer whether he backs Zelensky to win any election.

Zelensky said he believed wartime elections would currently be too dangerous for Ukraine in remarks released on Sunday.

"I believe that in a war like this, elections as such are a huge risk," he said. "Elections right now are a tsunami for the country that will split Ukraine."

Experts have cited a number of obstacles to holding such a vote, including how soldiers, millions of Ukrainian refugees and people from occupied territories would vote, as well as disinformation threats from Russia.

Fedorov's video highlighting political corruption last week came the day before a money laundering investigation was announced into lawmakers and bankers.

Ukraine's anti-corruption bureau said it had uncovered a scheme to misappropriate more than $3m (£2.2m) in Ukrainian currency to pay bail for a former energy minister accused of money laundering.

Fedorov said the case raised questions about the president's awareness of potential corruption in his inner circle.

"Let him answer this question... I believe that he's ready for such questions....

reflection.en: The news of corruption allegations within a government reminds us that true leadership is founded on integrity. Proverbs 16:12 teaches that evil is an abomination to rulers, and a throne is established by righteousness. This principle underscores the vital importance of accountability and ethical governance for any nation, especially in times of challenge.

title.en: Is the US seeing a turning point in obesity rates?

summary.en: Obesity rates climbed in the US for years, but now there are signs this could be changing. Use of weight-loss drugs such as Ozempic and Wegovy has increased rapidly — are they helping?
summary.zh: 这是一则来自全球栏目的新闻，重点涉及和平与克制。如需完整细节，请阅读英文原始报道。

body.en:
Obesity rates climbed in the US for years, but now there are signs this could be changing. Use of weight-loss drugs such as Ozempic and Wegovy has increased rapidly — are they helping?

The United States has been grappling with an obesity epidemic since the late 1970s, but there is growing evidence that the constantly climbing obesity rates are beginning to drop.

"We're seeing signs that there's going to be a turning point," said Benjamin Rader, an epidemiologist at Boston Children's Hospital and at Harvard Medical School who conducts research into health trends using large datasets. In 2024, he and his colleagues published a study based on data from more than 16 million adults, which suggested there had been a decline in obesity prevalence in 2023 — for the first time in more than 10 years.

The National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey also indicated a slight decline between 2021 and 2023. More recent surveys have also provided evidence of declining figures.

This comes as a series of new drugs, which some people are using for weight loss, have come onto the market. The use of the GLP-1 agonist drugs Ozempic, Wegovy and Zepbound has increased rapidly in recent years in the US, with prescriptions more than quadrupling between 2021 and early 2026.

Some of the active ingredients in these drugs were originally developed to treat Type 2 diabetes by mimicking a naturally occurring intestinal hormone to promote a feeling of fullness and to slow down gastric emptying. This has led to many patients losing a significant amount of weight.

For Rader, "it seemed like it [the impact of this medicine] was bound to show up in the data" and that it was possible to be "moderately confident that drugs themselves were having an effect."

For Peminda Cabandugama, an endocrinologist and spokesperson for The Obesity Society, which provides support to professionals in the obesity field, "there is strong evidence showing that there is a significant decline in obesity ."

In a written statement to DW, he said the "general opinion is that GLP-1 medications and their combinations and their increased use as well as the recent attention put on the importance of weight management have played a large and direct role in this reduction in obesity prevalence."

But for Rader there is no definitive proof of a causal relationship. He has no doubt that the drugs have led to weight loss in many people at an individual level, but he told DW that it was too soon to say whether it "will lead to a plateau, […] a decrease […] or a slower decrease in the next 20 years" and what the effect on the general population might be.

Cabandugama thinks the current figures might also have been influenced by lifestyle changes during and after the COVID-19 pandemic...

title.en: Iran-linked hackers blamed for cyber-attack that shut down UK power plant

summary.en: Incident marks apparent escalation by Tehran in its in retaliation against UK over allowing US to use British bases Hackers linked to Iran have been blamed for a cyber-attack that caused a British power plant to be temporarily shut down. The incident involved a small-scale...
summary.zh: 这是一则来自全球栏目的新闻，重点涉及和平与克制。如需完整细节，请阅读英文原始报道。

body.en:
Hackers linked to Iran have been blamed for a cyber-attack that caused a British power plant to be temporarily shut down.

The incident involved a small-scale energy generator, according to the UK government and at no point was there there risk to the wider energy system.

However, it marks an apparent escalation in the threat posed by Iran after the UK said it had given permission for the US to launch “defensive” operations against Tehran from British bases.

The power plant was shut down for four days as a result of the attack last month, according to the Sunday Telegraph , which first reported it.

A spokesperson for the Department for Energy Security and Net Zero said: “This story refers to an incident impacting a small-scale energy generator, and at no point was there a risk to the wider energy system. The UK has a highly resilient energy system. We work closely with the energy sector to protect infrastructure and ensure the highest security standards.”

The National Cyber Security Centre (NCSC), which deals with attacks on critical infrastructure, is understood not to have received any reported outages from regulated operators of power stations.

Hostile states such as Russia, China and Iran are increasingly targeting systems behind the UK’s key services, according to a warning this year from Richard Horne, the NCSC’s chief executive.

The government said last month the UK was “ready to defend itself” after Iran’s military warned any bases being used by the US were “legitimate targets” .

The UK has allowed the US to launch so-called defensive operations from British bases hosting American planes since the start of its war on Iran but has refused to help in offensive operations. That policy has not been altered by the new prime minister, Andy Burnham, who was notified last week that a decision had been made to extend the agreement with the US.

Iran’s Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) said last month that “any base used for aggression against Iranian territory constitutes a legitimate target for our forces”.

Iran has been accused for years of carrying out cyber-attacks on various countries, including in relation to a massive power outage in Turkey in 2015 and several possible breaches of Israeli government websites in 2022.

US government security agencies issued a warning earlier this year of cyber-attacks on critical infrastructure by hackers linked to the IRGC.

The US has alleged that an Iran-affiliated group known as “CyberAv3ngers” carried out a campaign against it in 2023 that compromised at least 75 devices in multiple infrastructure sectors.

title.en: Trump says Canada wants 'benefits' of being US state after trade talks collapse
title.zh: 特朗普称贸易谈判破裂后加拿大想获得成为美国州的“好处”

summary.en: Canada's Prime Minister said he was " reluctantly" announcing retaliatory tariffs and accused the US of starting a trade war.
summary.zh: 加拿大总理表示，他“不情愿地”宣布报复性关税，并指责美国挑起贸易战。

body.en:
US President Donald Trump has said Canada wants "the benefits of being a State, without being one" after trade talks between the two countries collapsed late on Friday.

In his first comments since negotiations broke down, triggering new 50% US tariffs on a range of Canadian goods, Trump also said American farmers had been charged "massive amounts of Tariffs" for years.

It comes after Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney called the fresh tariffs a "miscalculation" designed to "hurt and divide us".

Carney confirmed he would match Trump's tariffs "dollar-for-dollar" from 8 September, including levies on steel, dairy, appliances and electronics. The US and Canada are now in a trade "war", he said.

"They asked too much and they offered too little," Carney said on Saturday. "You're at war when you get attacked. We got attacked," he added.

Trump's latest comments echo his repeated references to making Canada the "51st state" of America since returning to office, sparking frustration among its leaders and residents.

The collapse of the trade talks upended a deeply integrated trading relationship, with no clear path to resolution.

"We cannot accept what they've offered, and we will not give what they've asked," Carney said.

Both countries were optimistic of a deal earlier in the week, but talks fell apart after both sides accused the other of making last-minute changes.

The new 50% US tariffs will apply to a range of Canadian goods, in addition to existing US tariffs on Canadian steel, aluminium, automobiles and lumber.

They are limited in scope, covering about $20bn (£15bn; C$28bn) of Canadian imports, or about 5% in total, including wine, dairy, cement, clothing and hockey equipment.

The prime minister said Canada was retaliating "reluctantly" to protect its interests. Details of the counter-measures will be released in the coming days, he said.

Leaders of other federal parties in Canada, including the Conservative opposition, voiced support for the prime minister, as have the leaders of some Canadian provinces.

Tariffs - a tax placed on imports from other countries - have been a key component of Trump's trade policy, with the US president arguing they will boost American manufacturing and create jobs at home.

Critics, however, say tariffs have raised prices for American consumers and have disrupted and damaged the global economy.

Carney's speech on Saturday was his first address to Canadians after he announced late on Friday night that a deal would not be reached, accusing the Americans of making "last-minute changes" that were "unfair" and "uneconomic".

US negotiators, meanwhile, accused Canada of making "new demands and walk backs" on terms which had been previously agreed.

title.en: Ukraine: Could ex-defense minister challenge Zelenskyy?
title.zh: 乌克兰：前国防部长能否挑战泽连斯基？

summary.en: Former Ukrainian defense minister Mykhailo Fedorov recently released a video criticizing corruption, leadership issues, and the state of elections in Ukraine. His comments have initiated a broad public discussion.
summary.zh: 乌克兰前国防部长米哈伊洛·费多罗夫最近发布了一段视频，批评了乌克兰的腐败、领导力危机和选举状况。他的言论引发了广泛的公众辩论。

body.en:
Last week, former Ukrainian defense minister Mykhailo Fedorov released a video in which he spoke of corruption, a crisis of leadership and elections. His explosive remarks have sparked widespread public debate.

This week, Ukraine was rocked by a series of political scandals. A month after stepping down as defense minister, Mykhailo Fedorov addressed the Ukrainian people in a nine-minute speech posted on his YouTube channel.

In his video message, he declares that Ukraine "cannot remain without a fully appointed minister of defense." But, he continues, "the main problem goes much deeper than one position or one ministry."

He says Ukraine's greatest challenge is a "systemic crisis of governance," of which corruption is only a symptom. Fedorov also criticized the fact that no national elections have been held in Ukraine since 2019.

A few hours earlier, the Ukrainian president, Volodymyr Zelenskyy , had proposed Yevhenii Khmara to parliament as the new defense minister. Khmara had been made acting minister of defense on July 20, and parliament confirmed him in the position on August 19.

When Fedorov spoke of corruption in government authorities, he may not have known about the scandal that would break the very day after he published his speech. On August 19, Ukrainian anti-corruption investigators searched the premises of several high-ranking officials, including a presidential deputy chief of staff, Iryna Mudra, and a member of parliament, Vadym Stolar.

Ukraine's National Anti-Corruption Bureau (NABU) stated that it was "conducting a special operation to expose a criminal organization" in conjunction with the Specialized Anti-Corruption Prosecutor's Office.

According to the investigating authorities, this organization was led by a current and a former Ukrainian lawmaker, and involved senior officials from the president's office. Volodymyr Zelenskyy dismissed Mudra from her post as presidential deputy chief of staff the same day.

In his video, Mykhailo Fedorov warns that "it is especially dangerous when society feels that the main criterion for appointing a person is not their professionalism, results, or ability […] but their personal loyalty to the system." He says that a "legal, safe, and realistic mechanism" needs to be found to make it possible to hold elections, even if Russia's war against Ukraine  continues for a long time.

The president dismissed Fedorov from his post as defense minister on July 15. Protests calling for his reinstatement began the following day in Kyiv, Lviv, Dnipro, Kharkiv, Zaporizhzhia, and other cities. title.en: Mexican governor facing US drug charges says leaving office
title.zh: 墨西哥州长面临美国毒品指控，称将离职

summary.en: Ruben Rocha Moya, the governor of Sinaloa state, has requested another leave of absence shortly after resuming his duties, following his entanglement in drug trafficking charges.
summary.zh: 锡那罗亚州州长鲁本·罗查·莫亚在因贩毒指控而卷入争议后，于重返岗位几天后再次申请休假。

body.en:
Embroiled in drug trafficking charges, Ruben Rocha Moya has asked for another leave of absence just days after returning to his position as Sinaloa state governor.

A Mexican state govenor, who is wanted by the US for conspiracy to smuggle drugs, says he sought a temporary but indefinite leave of absence just days after his controversial return to office.

"Sinaloa, the nation, and the movement of transformation are above everything," Sinaloa Governor Ruben Rocha Moya said in a post on X while sharing a document asking the state congress to authortize a "temporary leave of absence of indefinite duration, exceeding 30 days." 

Just one day earlier, the politician had announced on X that he was resuming state leadership of Sinaloa. The 77-year-old had stepped away from his position in May to face an investigation by Mexican prosecutors.

In April, US prosecutors alleged that Rocha and nine other current or former officials of the ruling Morena Party conspired with a faction of the Sinaloa Cartel to traffic drugs into the US in exchange for bribes and political support. It was the first time the US publicly charged a sitting Mexican politician.

Rocha has consistently denied the charges and implied that accusations against him are an attempt to harm the left-leaning Morena party.

Rocha's return announcement was not well received in the government or within his own Morena Party. Mexican President Claudia Sheinbaum on said "no personal interest can ever be placed above the interest of the people and the nation."

"Power without principles becomes arrogance; power without limits, abuse; and power that forgets the people ends up confronting history," she said, adding that Mexico deserved public servants who were not there to "feed personal ambitions."

Rocha was considered an ally of Sheinbaum and is very close to her mentor, former president Andres Manuel Lopez Obrador.

title.en: Kazakhstan's future after the elections: Russia, EU or China

summary.en: Kazakhstan, where power is being continuously consolidated in the president's hands, will have to continue its tough balancing act between the EU, Russia and China following the parliamentary elections this Sunday.
summary.zh: 这是一则来自全球栏目的新闻，重点涉及领导、智慧与公共责任。如需完整细节，请阅读英文原始报道。

body.en:
Kazakhstan, where power is being continuously consolidated in the president's hands, will have to continue its tough balancing act between the EU, Russia and China following the parliamentary elections this Sunday.

On August 23, Kazakhstan , a former Soviet country that has recently adopted a new constitution, will hold elections to its parliament.

The legislative body will be transformed from a two-chamber to a single-chamber system. Citizens will elect 145 members of parliament via party lists. All seven registered parties have been admitted to the election, including the ruling party, Adilet (which translates to "Justice").

But the election result is the least of the campaign's intrigues. Experts DW interviewed agree that no party other than President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev's Adilet stands a chance of winning.

Luca Anceschi, Professor of Eurasian Studies at the University of Glasgow, Scotland, suggests that the new parliament will do the same as the previous one, "which is pretty much to represent whatever the regime wants them to do."

In his view, one should not expect representatives of the genuine opposition to be elected to parliament.

Stefan Meister, Head of the Center for Order and Governance in Eastern Europe, Russia and Central Asia at the German Council on Foreign Relations (DGAP), shares this assessment. He says the ruling party is likely to win the election, a scenario also reflected in recent opinion polls. 

Both experts agree that these elections are intended to consolidate Tokayev's power and further weaken the bloc led by   Nursultan Nazarbayev , the country's president from 1991-2019. 

Constitutional amendments approved earlier allow Tokayev to seek another seven-year presidential term in 2029 and replace the two-chamber parliament with a single-chamber assembly called the Kurultai.

According to former Kazakhstani senator Zauresh Battalova, who now heads the NGO Foundation for the Development of Parliamentarism in Kazakhstan, what matters is not the number of chambers in parliament, but "the scope of its powers, its autonomy and its ability to oversee the executive branch of government."

The new constitution has changed not only the structure of parliament but also the way its members are elected. Independent candidates are no longer allowed to run under the current electoral system. Zauresh Battalova sees this as one of the factors limiting voters' political choice.

"The election will be held exclusively on the basis of party lists, in the absence of a political opposition and with limited party competition. The scope for genuine political choice remains extremely narrow," she told DW.

Meister and Anceschi both say that one should not expect any reaction...

reflection.en: This story draws attention to leadership, wisdom, and public responsibility. Proverbs 11:14 reminds us to meet sharp headlines with wisdom, integrity, and service, asking how faithful people can respond with wisdom instead of noise.
reflection.zh: 这则新闻让人想到领导、智慧与公共责任。Proverbs 11:14提醒我们，在快速变化的新闻里，仍要以智慧、正直与服事来回应，并学习用祷告与分辨代替情绪化判断。

verse.textEn: For lack of guidance a nation falls, but victory is won through many advisers.
verse.textZh: 无智谋，民就败落；谋士多，人便安居。

title.en: 'We're not going to run from it': Sydney Marathon laughs off medal error
title.zh: “我们不会逃避”：悉尼马拉松对奖牌错误一笑置之

summary.en: Runners participating in the Sydney Marathon will receive medals for the 2026 event that mistakenly feature an engraving of a German stadium. Organizers have acknowledged the error and are reportedly taking it in good humor.
summary.zh: 参加悉尼马拉松的跑者将在2026年收到一枚奖牌，上面错误地刻有德国体育场的图案。组织者已承认这一错误，并据报道以幽默的态度应对。

body.en:
The organisers of Sydney Marathon have laughed off a mistake which saw a German stadium etched on to medals for participants, saying "we're not going to run from it".

Questions arose after the event's official social media account unveiled the design of this year's medal earlier in the week, which had mistakenly etched Allianz Arena, based in the German city of Munich, instead of Sydney's Allianz Stadium.

A spokesperson for the Sydney Marathon told the BBC: "A little too much international flavour has found its way onto the back of the finishers medal, with an incorrect depiction of the stadium."

Recognisable Sydney landmarks feature on the double-sided medal, including the Opera House and Harbour Bridge, which are part of the 42.2km (26.2 mile) course.

Users on social media noticed the shape of the stadium engraved on the medal appeared to be carved in the wrong likeness.

Munich's Allianz Arena is sculpted by thousands of diamond-shaped inflatable cushions, while Sydney's similarly named Allianz Stadium has a flatter facade smoothed with long bronze fins.

Sydney Marathon confirmed runners would receive the medal depicting the incorrect city's stadium, noting: "It's a beautiful medal, and now a little more unique."

"It's certainly given everyone something to talk about this weekend, mostly in good humour."

Germany's Allianz Arena also poked fun at the mistake, writing on Instagram: "Oh wow, we didn't have that on our bingo card!"

"Perhaps they tried to find something else they had in common: Allianz Arena -- Sydney Opera -- Unique Architecture -- Both are worth a visit!"

The reverse side of the Sydney Marathon medal shows a gold and indigo pattern designed by First Nations artist Ambrose Killian, widely commended for its ornate pattern.

He confirmed to the BBC that he was not involved in designing the other face of the medal engraved with the wrong stadium.

Some 40,000 runners will take part in the event on 30 August, following more than 120,000 ballot entries.

reflection.en: Even in minor mishaps, our response reveals much about our character. The Sydney Marathon organizers' good-humored approach to a medal error, and their commitment to rectify it, reminds us that faithfulness extends to the smallest details. Yahweh calls us to integrity in all things, showing that even a small mistake can be handled with grace and a long-term...
reflection.zh: 即使是微小的失误，我们的回应也能展现出我们的品格。悉尼马拉松组织者以幽默的态度处理奖牌错误，并承诺纠正，这提醒我们忠诚体现在最小的细节中。雅伟呼召我们在一切事上保持正直，表明即使是小错误也可以用恩典和长远的眼光来处理。

verse.textEn: Whoever can be trusted with very little can also be trusted with much, and whoever is dishonest with very little will also be dishonest with much.
verse.textZh: 人在最小的事上忠心，在大事上也忠心；在最小的事上不义，在大事上也不义。

title.en: Girl, 17, killed in Swedish sword attack, police say
title.zh: 警方称瑞典持剑袭击受害者是一名17岁女孩

summary.en: Police in Sweden have identified the victim of a recent sword attack as a 17-year-old girl. Two boys, aged 12 and 17, were also injured in the incident, and an 18-year-old suspect has been detained.
summary.zh: 瑞典警方称，一名17岁女孩在最近的持剑袭击中丧生。两名分别为12岁和17岁的男孩也在袭击中受伤，一名18岁嫌疑人已被拘留。

body.en:
A 17-year-old girl was killed in the deadly sword attack at a high school in central Sweden on Friday, police have confirmed.

Two boys aged 12 and 17 were also seriously injured in the attack at Brinell School in Fagersta, according to local authorities, while another person sustained minor injuries.

An 18-year-old man was arrested but has not been identified. Police said they were treating the case as murder and attempted murder.

Swedish Prime Minister Ulf Kristersson and opposition leader Magdalena Andersson visited the school, where flower tributes have been laid to honour the victims, on Saturday morning.

Students at the school had only just returned to the classroom following the summer break when the deadly attack unfolded on Friday afternoon.

The police later confirmed they fired shots after being called to the scene but did not say whether the alleged attacker was hit before he was detained.

Sweden's public broadcaster reported that the suspect was wearing a helmet. Local media also said he was a former student.

The region went into a state of emergency on Friday, but it had ended by Saturday.

The school has just under 500 students on its roster, according to SVT, and is located 170km (105 miles) north-west of the capital, Stockholm.

Investigators have carried out two house searches in connection with the suspect, police said.

On Friday, Sweden's Prime Minister Ulf Kristersson described the attack as a "serious incident," and said "we do not know what lies behind the act, but we know that police are working very intensively", in a post on X.

Sweden's King Carl XVI Gustaf said he received the news "with dismay and sadness".

reflection.en: The tragic loss of a young life and the injury of others in this attack highlight the profound vulnerability of children and teenagers. Yahweh's word warns against causing harm to the innocent, reminding us of the sacred trust to protect the young among us. Such acts call us to grieve with those who mourn and to seek a world where all children can grow up...
reflection.zh: 这次袭击中年轻生命的悲惨逝去和另一些人的受伤，凸显了儿童和青少年极度的脆弱性。雅伟的话语警告我们不要伤害无辜者，提醒我们保护我们中间的年轻人是一项神圣的托付。此类行为呼唤我们与哀哭的人同哀哭，并寻求一个所有儿童都能免受暴力安全成长的世界。

title.en: What are Trump's options as US eyes 'never been seen' sanctions on Iran?
title.zh: 随着美国考虑对伊朗实施“前所未有”的制裁，特朗普有哪些选择？

summary.en: The head of Iran's supreme national security council has warned that any US action would lead to a confrontation "like an earthquake," as the US considers unprecedented sanctions.
summary.zh: 伊朗最高国家安全委员会负责人警告称，如果美国采取行动，对抗将“像地震一样”，此前美国正考虑对伊朗实施前所未有的制裁。

body.en:
US President Donald Trump has vowed to hit Iran hard economically, after treasury secretary Scott Bessent said that Washington would impose measures on Tehran that have "never been seen" as soon as next week.

The United States, ‌the United Nations and the European Union have applied sanctions, implemented trade embargoes and frozen Iranian assets since the late 1970s.

Since the US and Israel launched the war on Iran in February, Washington has levied additional maritime, energy and financial sanctions and started a naval blockade.

Iran — which has withstood decades of punishing sanctions — has denounced US plans to announce new sanctions and on Sunday warned countries against participating in the United States' "economic war" against the country.

Washington has pushed its allies to jump aboard Trump's new campaign to isolate the Iranian economy, as the US president's unpopular war drags toward the six-month mark.

"We declare to all countries ... do not join the economic war waged by the United States," said Mohsen Rezai, the head of Iran's supreme national security council, on Iranian television.

"Any country participating in the imposition of economic restrictions against us is considered an enemy."

Data from the US treasury department's Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) shows the agency has imposed sanctions on more than 1,000 people, vessels and aircraft since Trump began his second term.

Recent measures have targeted Iran's shadow oil fleet; shipping insurers; entities and people enabling Iran's acquisition of weapons; and digital exchanges, freezing an estimated US$500 billion ($697 billion) in Iran-linked cryptocurrency.

Oil shipments are at a virtual standstill in the Strait of Hormuz, with Tehran threatening to strike any unauthorised oil tankers that try to transit the vital waterway.

Chinese independent refineries known as "teapots" account for a quarter of Chinese refinery capacity. They operate with narrow and sometimes negative profit margins.

China buys more than 80 per cent of Iran's shipped oil, according to 2025 data from analytics firm Kpler. Independent refiners absorb much of this trade, exposing them to so-called secondary measures that penalise entities helping a primary sanctions target.

Past US sanctions have deterred larger independent refiners from buying Iranian oil. But the independent refineries are somewhat immune since they have little exposure to the US financial system, sanctions experts say.

Yet, Scripture reminds us that Yahweh has not given us a spirit of fear, but of power, love, and self-control. This calls leaders to approach complex situations with strength, compassion, and wise restraint, rather than succumbing to escalatory...

title.en: Canada's Carney stands up to Trump in an escalating trade war. Could his gamble pay off?
title.zh: 加拿大卡尼在不断升级的贸易战中对抗特朗普。他的赌注能成功吗？

summary.en: Mark Carney was elected last year on a promise to be a tough negotiator with Trump, and remains broadly popular in Canada.
summary.zh: 马克·卡尼去年当选时承诺将成为与特朗普的强硬谈判者，他在加拿大仍然广受欢迎。

body.en:
Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney announced retaliatory tariffs on the United States on Sunday, after walking away from a "bad deal" on trade in a deepening rift between the longtime allies.

Negotiations between the neighbouring countries broke down on Saturday in Washington, triggering new 50 per cent US tariffs that will affect about US$20 billion ($27.9 billion) worth of goods, or 5.5 per cent of Canadian exports to the United States.

Carney then announced retaliatory duties on US goods, notably steel and dairy products, to take effect on 8 September.

Although Carney stood up to US President Donald Trump by rejecting what he called an "unfair" trade deal, this gamble could prove economically risky.

Canada has been seeking relief from Trump's tariffs on autos, steel and aluminium, which have battered the country's economy, forced job losses and strained what was once an iron-clad trade relationship.

The White House had alleged "discriminatory treatment" by Canada against US alcohol, automobile and dairy products in introducing the duties.

Trump had said Washington "should be able to have a deal with Canada," citing his "good relationship" with Carney.

But on Saturday, Canada's prime minister said Trump set conditions that were ultimately unacceptable even though earlier talks had been positive.

"In recent days, the United States proposed new terms that were uneconomic, unfair and undermined the net benefits for Canada, and called into question the reliability of any deal," Carney said in Ottawa.

"We cannot accept what they've offered, and we will not give what they've asked."

"Our government understood before many that America would transform all of its commercial relationships, that it would put a series of tariffs on its closest allies, and use economic integration as a weapon," Carney said on Saturday.

He pledged that his country would match the US tariffs "dollar for dollar to protect our workers and businesses".

Carney, the former head of the central banks of Canada and Britain, earned full support across Canada's political spectrum, with opposition leader Pierre Poilievre calling on citizens to "stand united to defend our country against these unfair attacks on our jobs and businesses."

The Globe and Mail, in an editorial, said: "In the end, Prime Minister Mark Carney took the hint from the Canadian public rather than the bait from the US president."

A poll published earlier in the week revealed that 56 per cent of Canadians surveyed wanted their government to take a "hard line" and make no more concessions to the US on trade.

Proverbs 11:14 reminds us that a nation thrives when its leaders seek and receive abundant wise counsel. title.en: Sam was sent to prison during China's crackdown in Hong Kong. He returned to a city in silence
title.zh: 香港镇压异见，山姆出狱后发现城市一片寂静

summary.en: Six years after China imposed the National Security Law, Hong Kong's crackdown on dissent has spread beyond its borders.
summary.zh: 中国实施《国家安全法》六年之后，香港对异见的镇压已蔓延至境外。

body.en:
Watch Dateline’s latest episode, Hong Kong: A City Silenced, on 25 August at 9.30pm AEST on SBS or SBS On Demand.

At 21, Sam Chan Chi-sum was preparing to leave Hong Kong to continue his studies overseas.

He'd been involved with a student activist group that collected sweets and toiletries to send to people jailed after Hong Kong’s 2019 anti-government protests.

Authorities accused the group of using the supplies to build support among prisoners and incite opposition to the government.

Your trusted source for staying up-to-date with the world around you. Get free daily news updates and analysis, straight to your inbox.

In September 2021, Sam was arrested under Hong Kong’s sweeping National Security Law, which had been passed a year earlier, and was convicted of "subversion with the intent of overthrowing the government".

"Prison was awful. I shared a cell with around twenty people. At its most crowded, there could be forty of us," he said.

He alleged some prison officers purposely mistreated inmates associated with the protest movement.

"I don't know whether they were acting out of personal conviction or following orders. But they certainly made life difficult for us."

Two years after his release from prison, Sam is trying to rebuild a normal life.

He had dreamt of becoming a teacher or a nurse, but his criminal record prevents him from pursuing either career.

"Since being released from prison, I feel as though I've entered a much larger cell," he said.

Instead, he is training to become a documentary filmmaker, determined, he says, to capture the transformation of Hong Kong.

"Whatever the outcome for Hong Kong, whether the future is good or bad, I want to stay here and witness the changes that lie ahead."

Sam’s story is like many other young Hongkongers whose lives have been upended by China’s crackdown on freedoms in Hong Kong, a city once known for its outspoken press, independent judiciary and political opposition.

In 1997, after more than 150 years of British rule, Hong Kong was handed back to China under the "one country, two systems" arrangement that promised Hong Kong would keep a high degree of autonomy.

Like Sam, Carmen Lau was from a generation that came of age after this handover to China: neither British, nor truly Chinese.

As a teenager, Carmen led a student movement in her secondary school against the Chinese Communist Party's (CCP) attempt to introduce 'patriotism' lessons in Hong Kong schools.

Many Hongkongers feared it would promote the CCP’s version of patriotism in their city.

"That time was the first time that I was really involved in a social event," said Lau, who’s now 30 and lives in exile in London.

Following large demonstrations, the CCP abandoned its plans...

reflection.en: The story of Sam returning to a silenced city after imprisonment highlights the profound impact of oppressive rule on a community. Yahweh's word reminds us that a wicked ruler can be like a roaring lion, bringing fear and helplessness to the people. In such times, we are called to remember the dignity of every individual and pray for justice and peace.
reflection.zh: 山姆在被囚禁后回到一个寂静的城市，这个故事凸显了压迫性统治对一个社区的深远影响。雅伟的话语提醒我们，邪恶的统治者如同咆哮的狮子，给人民带来恐惧和无助。在这样的时刻，我们被呼召要记住每个人的尊严，并为公义与和平祷告。

verse.textEn: Like a roaring lion or a charging bear is a wicked ruler over a helpless people.
verse.textZh: 暴虐的君王辖制贫民，好像吼叫的狮子、觅食的熊。

title.en: Spain battles forest fire a short drive from flash flood
title.zh: 西班牙在洪水爆发地附近奋力扑灭森林大火

summary.en: A forest fire near Valencia, Spain, forced over 1,000 residents from their homes, while in nearby Catalonia, flash floods necessitated 200 rescue operations for people trapped in cars and houses.
summary.zh: 西班牙瓦伦西亚附近的一场森林大火迫使1000多人撤离家园，而在邻近的加泰罗尼亚，洪水导致200起救援行动，居民被困在汽车和房屋中。

body.en:
The blaze, near Valencia, forced more than 1,000 people from their homes. In nearby Catalonia, civil defense teams carried out 200 rescue operations after floods trapped residents in cars and homes.

A forest fire in eastern Spain sparked the evacuation of around 1,000 people on Saturday, authorities said.

The blaze is one of hundreds that firefighters across Europe have been battling this summer amid record high temperatures along the Mediterranean and elsewhere.

Barely 150 kilometers (93 miles) away on the Costa Dorada, flash floods trapped people in cars, toppled walls and forced the evacuation of a campsite.

The fire is burning close to Gatova, an inland village with a population of 450, northwest of Valencia.

Spain's Military Emergency Unit UME posted a video to X showing its firefighters working in the darkness to douse the flames.

Local media reported that the blaze is thought to have been started by a lightning strike late Thursday.

Juan Carlos Valderrama, Valencia autonomous community's civil protection minister, said buses were on standby to help residents without their own vehicles to leave their homes.

Further north, along Spain's Costa Dorada, heavy rain overnight flooded streets and caused the collapse of two walls, injuring at least seven people, officials said. 

According to local media, roads in the coastal towns El Vendrell, Coma-ruga and Torredembarra in the Catalonia region were partially submerged.

The Meteorological Service of Catalonia said several towns recorded nearly 200 liters per square meter in just a few hours.

On Saturday morning, the agency warned of more heavy rainfall for the coastal region.

Local media reported that several people got trapped in their vehicles during the flooding.

A regional emergency official said firefighters had carried out more than 200 missions to rescue people from vehicles and flooded buildings.

summary.en: Scores of villagers have been killed and abducted in central Nigeria following deadly clashes between rival jihadist factions.

body.en:
Jihadists kidnapped and killed scores of people in an attack during Friday prayers in central Nigeria's Niger state.

Survivors and lawmakers told the Agence-France Presse (AFP) news agency on Saturday that some people managed to escape during a clash with rival militants.

Africa's most populous country is battling a 17-year insurgency by jihadist groups, which have made mass abductions a key tactic — including the 2014 kidnapping of hundreds of schoolgirls in the town of Chibok.

The insurgency is concentrated in the northeast, though Friday's attack was near the western border with Benin, an area that has seen increased activity by local armed groups and militants from the neighbouring Sahel as the conflict has splintered.

"Soon after finishing the normal Friday prayer, the armed group of Lakuwara, in their hundreds, wielding guns, knives and machetes, began to attack us," said Jibril Ahmad, who survived the attack on Dikera village, in the Borgu local government area.

"They slaughtered some of our people, saying we are not practicing the true teachings of Islam," Ahmad said.

The nearby village of Binzi was also hit, Ahmad and federal representative Jafaru Mohammed told AFP.

Lakurawa is a shadowy group that some researchers have linked to Islamic State Sahel Province. ISSP is active in Burkina Faso, Mali and Niger.

Amid the violence, another jihadist group, known as Mahmuda, intervened and clashed with the Lakurawa fighters, Ahmad and Mohammed said.

"Many of us have escaped, while they were busy trying to confront" the Mahmuda fighters, Ahmad said.

Mohammed told AFP that "some members of the Mahmuda group were against the doctrine of the Lakurawa and when they heard of what the Lakurawa were doing they fought them."

"But as of now many of our people have been slaughtered and many have been kidnapped and taken into the bushes," he said.

Police in Niger state said they were aware of the kidnapping, but had not received reports of anyone killed.

In August last year, the Nigerian government claimed it had "dismantled" Mahmuda and another group, Ansaru, with the arrest of their leaders.

Though jihadist violence in Nigeria has declined since its peak around a decade ago, during the height of jihadist group Boko Haram's insurgency, the military and police remain overstretched as they face multiple, sometimes overlapping conflicts.

Northwest and central Nigeria, where jihadists have been making inroads, are also awash with non-ideological "bandit" gangs that raid villages, conduct kidnappings and "tax" farmers and miners.

title.en: Kazakhstan's future after the elections: Russia, EU or China
title.zh: 哈萨克斯坦选举后的未来：俄罗斯、欧盟还是中国

summary.en: Kazakhstan's parliamentary elections will be followed by the nation continuing its complex geopolitical balancing act between the EU, Russia, and China, amidst ongoing consolidation of presidential power.
summary.zh: 哈萨克斯坦议会选举后，该国总统权力持续巩固，将继续在欧盟、俄罗斯和中国之间进行艰难的平衡。

body.en:
Kazakhstan, where power is being continuously consolidated in the president's hands, will have to continue its tough balancing act between the EU, Russia and China following the parliamentary elections this Sunday.

On August 23, Kazakhstan , a former Soviet country that has recently adopted a new constitution, will hold elections to its parliament.

The legislative body will be transformed from a two-chamber to a single-chamber system. Citizens will elect 145 members of parliament via party lists. All seven registered parties have been admitted to the election, including the ruling party, Adilet (which translates to "Justice").

But the election result is the least of the campaign's intrigues. Experts DW interviewed agree that no party other than President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev's Adilet stands a chance of winning.

Luca Anceschi, Professor of Eurasian Studies at the University of Glasgow, Scotland, suggests that the new parliament will do the same as the previous one, "which is pretty much to represent whatever the regime wants them to do."

In his view, one should not expect representatives of the genuine opposition to be elected to parliament.

Stefan Meister, Head of the Center for Order and Governance in Eastern Europe, Russia and Central Asia at the German Council on Foreign Relations (DGAP), shares this assessment. He says the ruling party is likely to win the election, a scenario also reflected in recent opinion polls. 

Both experts agree that these elections are intended to consolidate Tokayev's power and further weaken the bloc led by   Nursultan Nazarbayev , the country's president from 1991-2019. 

Constitutional amendments approved earlier allow Tokayev to seek another seven-year presidential term in 2029 and replace the two-chamber parliament with a single-chamber assembly called the Kurultai.

According to former Kazakhstani senator Zauresh Battalova, who now heads the NGO Foundation for the Development of Parliamentarism in Kazakhstan, what matters is not the number of chambers in parliament, but "the scope of its powers, its autonomy and its ability to oversee the executive branch of government."

The new constitution has changed not only the structure of parliament but also the way its members are elected. Independent candidates are no longer allowed to run under the current electoral system. Zauresh Battalova sees this as one of the factors limiting voters' political choice.

"The election will be held exclusively on the basis of party lists, in the absence of a political opposition and with limited party competition. The scope for genuine political choice remains extremely narrow," she told DW.

Meister and Anceschi both say that one should not expect any reaction...

reflection.en: As Kazakhstan navigates its complex geopolitical landscape and consolidates presidential power, the need for wise counsel and broad guidance becomes paramount. A nation's stability and well-being are often found not in concentrated power alone, but in the collective wisdom that ensures safety and sound direction.

title.en: Sam was sent to prison during China's crackdown in Hong Kong. He returned to a city in silence
title.zh: 香港镇压异见，山姆出狱后发现城市一片寂静

summary.en: Six years after China imposed the National Security Law, Hong Kong's crackdown on dissent has spread beyond its borders.
summary.zh: 中国实施《国家安全法》六年之后，香港对异见的镇压已蔓延至境外。

body.en:
Watch Dateline’s latest episode, Hong Kong: A City Silenced, on 25 August at 9.30pm AEST on SBS or SBS On Demand.

At 21, Sam Chan Chi-sum was preparing to leave Hong Kong to continue his studies overseas.

He'd been involved with a student activist group that collected sweets and toiletries to send to people jailed after Hong Kong’s 2019 anti-government protests.

Authorities accused the group of using the supplies to build support among prisoners and incite opposition to the government.

In September 2021, Sam was arrested under Hong Kong’s sweeping National Security Law, which had been passed a year earlier, and was convicted of "subversion with the intent of overthrowing the government".

"Prison was awful. I shared a cell with around twenty people. At its most crowded, there could be forty of us," he said.

He alleged some prison officers purposely mistreated inmates associated with the protest movement.

"I don't know whether they were acting out of personal conviction or following orders. But they certainly made life difficult for us."

Two years after his release from prison, Sam is trying to rebuild a normal life.

He had dreamt of becoming a teacher or a nurse, but his criminal record prevents him from pursuing either career.

"Since being released from prison, I feel as though I've entered a much larger cell," he said.

Instead, he is training to become a documentary filmmaker, determined, he says, to capture the transformation of Hong Kong.

"Whatever the outcome for Hong Kong, whether the future is good or bad, I want to stay here and witness the changes that lie ahead."

Sam’s story is like many other young Hongkongers whose lives have been upended by China’s crackdown on freedoms in Hong Kong, a city once known for its outspoken press, independent judiciary and political opposition.

In 1997, after more than 150 years of British rule, Hong Kong was handed back to China under the "one country, two systems" arrangement that promised Hong Kong would keep a high degree of autonomy.

Like Sam, Carmen Lau was from a generation that came of age after this handover to China: neither British, nor truly Chinese.

As a teenager, Carmen led a student movement in her secondary school against the Chinese Communist Party's (CCP) attempt to introduce 'patriotism' lessons in Hong Kong schools.

Many Hongkongers feared it would promote the CCP’s version of patriotism in their city.

"That time was the first time that I was really involved in a social event," said Lau, who’s now 30 and lives in exile in London.

Following large demonstrations, the CCP abandoned its plans...

reflection.en: The story of Sam returning to a silenced city after imprisonment highlights the profound impact of oppressive rule on a community. Yahweh's word reminds us that a wicked ruler can be like a roaring lion, bringing fear and helplessness to the people. In such times, we are called to remember the dignity of every individual and pray for justice and peace.

title.en: Watch: Moment humanoid robot beats Usain Bolt's 100m record
title.zh: 观看：人形机器人打破博尔特百米纪录的瞬间

summary.en: A humanoid robot has set a new 100-meter dash record, completing the distance in 9.39 seconds at the World Humanoid Robot Games in Beijing, surpassing Usain Bolt's previous human record.
summary.zh: 在北京举行的世界人形机器人运动会上，一个人形机器人以9.39秒的成绩跑完100米，打破了尤塞恩·博尔特此前保持的人类纪录。

body.en:
A robot has outperformed humans by running faster than Usain Bolt's 100m sprint world record at the World Humanoid Robot Games in China.

The humanoid robot, developed by the Beijing Innovation Centre of Humanoid Robotics, ran the distance in 9.39 seconds at the event.

Eight-time Olympic gold medallist Bolt set the world record for humans in 2009, running 100m in 9.58 seconds.

The robot beat two others including one made by Chinese smartphone maker Honor - which the manufacturer says ran the distance in 9.32 seconds in a test run.

Other events at the robot games, which started on Saturday, include boxing and football, but also household tasks such as folding laundry.

reflection.en: The news of a robot surpassing a human athletic record invites us to consider the nature of achievement. While technological advancements are remarkable, the apostle Paul reminds us that earthly crowns are perishable. Our ultimate pursuit is for an eternal crown, found not in fleeting records but in a life lived for Yahweh.
reflection.zh: 机器人打破人类运动纪录的消息，促使我们思考成就的本质。虽然科技进步令人惊叹，但使徒保罗提醒我们，地上的冠冕是会朽坏的。我们最终的追求是那永恒的冠冕，它不在于转瞬即逝的纪录，而在于为雅伟而活的生命。

A robot horse and dancing humanoids are among the machines that have been showcased by Chinese manufacturers at a conference in Beijing.

The five-day 2026 World Robot Conference, which started on Wednesday, comes as the country continues to expand its robotics industry.

On the day the conference kicked off, the world's biggest humanoid robot maker Unitree Robotics made its stock market debut in Shanghai.

As we marvel at these advancements, we are reminded to seek wisdom in how...
reflection.zh: 北京会议上机器人技术的精彩展示，彰显了人类非凡的创造力以及科技进步的加速步伐。但以理书12:4所预言的知识的快速增长，邀请我们思考这些创新所带来的深远影响。当我们惊叹于这些进步时，也提醒我们要以智慧来开发和应用这些强大的工具。

title.en: Would even an AI disaster on the scale of Hiroshima be enough to make humankind protect itself? I fear not | Timothy Garton Ash
title.zh: 蒂莫西·加顿·阿什：即使是广岛规模的人工智能灾难，也足以让人类保护自己吗？我恐怕不会

summary.en: The article expresses concern from Silicon Valley experts that Artificial Intelligence is developing at a pace exceeding humanity's capacity to control it. The author fears that even a catastrophic AI event might not prompt sufficient self-protective measures from humankind.
summary.zh: 文章表达了硅谷专家对人工智能发展速度超出人类控制能力的担忧。作者担心，即使发生一场人工智能灾难，人类可能也无法采取足够的自我保护措施。

body.en: It’s clear here in Silicon Valley that AI is advancing faster than humans’ ability to control it. That means even sober prophecies seem optimistic Here in Silicon Valley, the experts think that within the next couple of years we’ll see an extraordinary takeoff for artificial intelligence. “Welcome to the foothills of the singularity,” as a Stanford University friend greeted me. More prosaically, the imminent breakthrough is described as “recursive self-improvement” – the point at which AI itself trains each successive model of AI, resulting in an exponential development to something which, in many significant respects, is more intelligent than us humans. As Robert Wright puts it in his book The God Test : “Never before has the near-term future … held such a wide array of not-implausible paths for humankind that would be so wildly transformative.” But will this be heaven or hell? Heaven, says Elon Musk, who predicts “an age of amazing abundance” – although he also sees a 10-20% chance of killer robots murdering us all. Hell is more likely according to Geoffrey Hinton , one of the intellectual founding fathers of AI. “My intuition is, we’re toast,” he told an interviewer in 2023. And talking to Sebastian Mallaby , author of The Infinity Machine, a book about the quest for superintelligence, Hinton estimates p(doom) – the probability of human extinction – at 50%, “because I haven’t got a clue how to estimate the real number”. “As soon as evolution [of AI] kicks in, we’re fucked,” he adds cheerfully. But whether it’s God or Godzilla, artificial superintelligence is just around the corner. Timothy Garton Ash is a Guardian columnist Continue reading...
body.zh: 在硅谷，人工智能的发展速度明显快于人类控制它的能力。这意味着即使是清醒的预言也显得乐观。在硅谷，专家们认为，在未来几年内，我们将看到人工智能的非凡腾飞。 “欢迎来到奇点的山麓，”一位斯坦福大学的朋友向我打招呼。更通俗地说，即将到来的突破被描述为“递归自我改进”——人工智能本身训练每个连续的人工智能模型，从而实现指数级发展，在许多重要方面比我们人类更聪明。正如罗伯特·赖特（Robert Wright）在他的《上帝的考验》一书中所说：“在不久的将来……从来没有为人类提供过如此广泛的并非难以置信的道路，并且具有如此巨大的变革性。”但这到底是天堂还是地狱呢？埃隆·马斯克 (Elon Musk) 表示，这是天堂，他预测“一个令人惊叹的丰富时代”，尽管他也认为杀手机器人有 10-20% 的可能性谋杀我们所有人。人工智能创始人之一杰弗里·辛顿 (Geoffrey Hinton) 认为，地狱更有可能发生。 “我的直觉是，我们完蛋了，”他在 2023 年对一位采访者说道。在与《无限机器》（一本关于探索超级智能的书）的作者 Sebastian Mallaby 交谈时，Hinton 估计 p(doom)——人类灭绝的概率——为 50%，“因为我不知道如何估计真实的数字”。 “一旦[人工智能]进化开始，我们就完蛋了，”他高兴地补充道。但无论是上帝还是哥斯拉，人工智能都指日可待。蒂莫西·加顿·阿什 (Timothy Garton Ash) 是《卫报》专栏作家继续阅读...

reflection.en: The rapid advancement of AI, as highlighted in this report, presents a profound challenge to human foresight and prudence. Proverbs 27:12 reminds us that the wise foresee danger and take refuge, while the naive press on and suffer the consequences. As we navigate these complex technological frontiers, may we seek the wisdom to discern potential harms and...
reflection.zh: 正如这篇报道所强调的，人工智能的迅速发展对人类的远见和审慎提出了严峻挑战。箴言27:12提醒我们，通达人预见危险就藏躲，愚蒙人却往前行，自受亏损。在我们探索这些复杂的技术前沿时，愿我们寻求智慧，辨明潜在的危害，并负责任地行动，以保护我们共同的未来。

verse.textEn: The prudent see danger and take refuge, but the simple keep going and pay the penalty.
verse.textZh: 通达人见祸藏躲；愚蒙人前往受害。

title.en: ‘She’s not afraid of anyone’: the prison writings of one of Hong Kong’s last outspoken democracy activists
title.zh: “她无所畏惧”：香港最后一位直言不讳的民主活动家之一的狱中手稿

Continue reading...

title.en: After two decades, China is preparing its boldest Moon mission yet
title.zh: 中国正准备执行二十年来最雄心勃勃的探月任务

summary.en: China is preparing its most ambitious moon mission in two decades, scheduled for next month. The mission aims to explore the lunar surface, specifically searching for water.
summary.zh: 中国正准备在下个月执行其二十年来最雄心勃勃的探月任务。此次任务旨在探索月球表面，特别是寻找水资源。

body.en:
How do you explore a place where the sun never shines? China's space program will soon embark on one of the most innovative lunar exploration missions in recent years.

We’ve known for nearly two decades that some form of water exists on the moon. What we still don’t know is exactly how much accessible water ice lies inside permanently shadowed craters, how deeply it is buried or what form it takes.

What we do know is that accessing that water ice will be a real challenge: it is found at the bottom of deep, hard-to-traverse craters where the sun never shines, remaining untouched for billions of years at temperatures well below –200C. These are among the most valuable places on the moon, but the hardest to reach and explore.

Lunar exploration has come a long way since the Soviet Union’s Luna-1 probe reached the moon's vicinity in January 1959. The Apollo missions and their successors showed the challenge is no longer simply to reach the moon. It is to explore places human and conventional rovers cannot easily go, and ultimately determine whether the moon itself can provide some of the resources that future explorers will need.

China has spent two decades building an increasingly ambitious lunar exploration program, named after Chang'e, the ancient Chinese goddess of the moon. The Chang'e-7 mission is expected to set course for our celestial neighbour later this month, although a recent failure involving a different Chinese rocket has introduced some uncertainty over the launch date. Here’s what makes this latest mission so interesting.

The mission will test several novel approaches to lunar exploration. It will consist of an orbiter, a lander, a rover and a hopper.

In addition, the Queqiao-2 lunar relay satellite is already in place. Launched separately in March 2024, it subsequently supported the Chang'e-6 mission and will facilitate communication between Earth and the lunar surface during the Chang'e-7 mission.

We don’t know precisely where the mission will land, but a site on or near an illuminated ridge close to the Shackleton crater in the Lunar South Pole’s Aitken region is a prime candidate.

The hopper will be the mission’s real star. Unlike a wheeled rover, it’s designed to leap over broken terrain and descend into craters where sunlight never reaches, places conventional vehicles may simply be unable to enter.

Adding it to the mission makes sense, given the steep crater walls, broken terrain, permanent shadow and the need for autonomous navigation and communications.

Chinese scientists won’t be looking for signs of water; we...
body.zh: 如何探索一个阳光照不到的地方？中国的太空计划很快将启动近年来最具创新性的月球探测任务之一。 近二十年来，我们已经知道月球上存在某种形式的水。我们仍然不知道的是，在永久阴影的陨石坑内到底有多少可接近的水冰，它埋藏的深度有多深，或者它的形式是什么。 我们所知道的是，获取这些水冰将是一个真正的挑战：它是在难以穿越的深坑底部发现的，那里的阳光永远不会照射到，在远低于零下200摄氏度的温度下数十亿年都保持不变。这些是月球上最有价值的地方，但也是最难到达和探索的地方。 自 1959 年 1 月苏联的 Luna-1 探测器到达月球附近以来，月球探索已经取得了长足的进步。阿波罗任务及其后续任务表明，挑战不再仅仅是到达月球。它是为了探索人类和传统漫游车无法轻易到达的地方，并最终确定月球本身是否可以提供未来探险者所需的一些资源。 中国花了二十年的时间制定了一项日益雄心勃勃的月球探测计划，该计划以中国古代月亮女神嫦娥的名字命名。嫦娥七号任务预计将于本月晚些时候飞往我们的天体邻居，尽管最近另一枚中国火箭的失败给发射日期带来了一些不确定性。这就是这个最新任务如此有趣的原因。 您值得信赖的来源，让您了解周围世界的最新动态。直接将免费的每日新闻更新和分析发送到您的收件箱。 该任务将测试几种月球探索的新方法。它将由轨道飞行器、着陆器、漫游车和漏斗组成。 此外，鹊桥二号月球中继卫星也已就位。它于2024年3月单独发射，随后支持嫦娥六号任务，并将在嫦娥七号任务期间促进地球与月球表面之间的通信。 我们不知道任务将在哪里着陆，但月球南极艾特肯地区靠近沙克尔顿陨石坑的照明山脊上或附近的一个地点是主要候选地点。 漏斗将成为这次任务的真正明星。与轮式漫游车不同，它的设计目的是跳过破碎的地形并下降到阳光永远无法到达的陨石坑中，而传统车辆可能根本无法进入这些地方。 考虑到陡峭的火山口壁、破碎的地形、永久的阴影以及自主导航和通信的需求，将其添加到任务中是有意义的。 中国科学家不会寻找水的迹象；而是寻找水的迹象。我们...

Psalm 8:4 invites us to ponder our worth in Yahweh's eyes, even as we marvel at the universe He created. This pursuit of knowledge beyond our planet can deepen our wonder at both the Creator and the unique dignity...
reflection.zh: 随着人类向太空深处迈进，中国探月任务等行动提醒我们，在浩瀚宇宙中，我们虽渺小却意义非凡。诗篇8:4邀请我们思考雅伟眼中我们的价值，即使我们惊叹于他所创造的宇宙。这种超越地球的知识探索，能加深我们对造物主以及他赐予我们独特尊严的敬畏。

title.en: Indonesia-China naval drill raises neutrality concerns
title.zh: 印尼与中国海军演习引发中立担忧

summary.en: Indonesia's participation in a limited naval exercise with China near Taiwan has raised questions about its long-standing nonaligned foreign policy.
summary.zh: 印度尼西亚与中国海军在台湾附近举行了有限的海上演习，这引发了对其长期不结盟外交政策的担忧。

body.en:
Indonesia maintains a nonaligned foreign policy, but Jakarta's limited participation in a low-level naval exercise with China's navy near Taiwan has drawn scrutiny.

On August 12, an Indonesian frigate briefly joined a naval exercise with China's People's Liberation Army Navy (PLAN) in waters off Taiwan's east coast, with Taipei asking Jakarta for a reason why it joined the drill.

Indonesian Navy frigate KRI I Gusti Ngurah Rai joined the PLAN guided-missile frigate Honghe for what Jakarta described as a "passing exercise." The maneuvers took place during Taiwan's annual Han Kuang military drill. 

An Indonesian Ministry of Foreign Affairs spokesperson said they were fully aware that the exercise's location "made it particularly sensitive," but stressed that its vessel's presence "was simply part of its transit route back to Indonesia." According to the Taipei Times , the Indonesian vessel was returning from Vladivostok, Russia after an exercise with the Russian navy.  

Taiwan's Mainland Affairs Council condemned Beijing's "provocation" after China announced the drill on August 11. Taipei also requested "further details from the Indonesian government" from its Ministry of Foreign Affairs.  

Beijing considers Taiwan to be Chinese territory and has vowed to "reunite" the self-ruled island with the mainland, by using force if necessary . The People's Liberation Army has ratcheted up pressure on Taiwan with frequent military exercises around the island, especially since former US House Speaker Nancy Pelosi visited Taipei in 2022.

Amid reactions from Taipei and Washington, the Indonesian Navy stated that its activities with the Chinese Navy were "not warfighting activities in nature" and "not intended as combat training."

Ying-Yu Lin, an associate professor at Taiwan's Tamkang University Graduate Institute of International Affairs and Strategic Studies, told DW that the Chinese exercise with Indonesia had little tactical significance.

"It wasn't as practical as a joint maritime drill, but China wanted to claim its capability in the waters," he said.

However, Ratih Kabinawa, a visiting research fellow at the Japan Institute of International Affairs focusing on Taiwan-Indonesia ties, told DW that regardless of the significance of the drills, Indonesia should have expected some reaction from Taiwan .

"Like it or not, Indonesia is now dragged into this kind of geopolitical gambit," she said.

Kabinawa added that passing exercises were among the lowest-level naval activities yet used by China to justify its intimidation of Taiwan.

"Indonesia must also exercise caution in this regard," she said, adding that Jakarta should "not to be too naive," to assume that its participation in a "regular exercise" with China would not cause concern in...
body.zh: 印度尼西亚维持不结盟的外交政策，但雅加达有限地参与与中国海军在台湾附近举行的低级别海军演习，引起了密切关注。 8月12日，一艘印度尼西亚护卫舰短暂参加了与中国人民解放军海军在台湾东海岸附近海域举行的海军演习，台北向雅加达询问其参加演习的原因。 印度尼西亚海军护卫舰 KRI I Gusti Ngurah Rai 与中国海军导弹护卫舰红河号一起进行了雅加达所说的“穿越演习”。这次演习是在台湾一年一度的汉光军演期间进行的。 印度尼西亚外交部发言人表示，他们完全意识到演习地点“使其特别敏感”，但强调其船只的存在“只是其返回印度尼西亚的过境路线的一部分”。据《台北时报》报道，这艘印尼舰艇在与俄罗斯海军演习后正从俄罗斯符拉迪沃斯托克返回。 中国8月11日宣布演习后，台湾陆委会谴责北京的“挑衅”。台北还要求外交部“提供更多细节”。 北京认为台湾是中国领土，并誓言要让这个自治岛屿与大陆“统一”，必要时会使用武力。特别是自美国前众议院议长南希·佩洛西 2022 年访问台北以来，解放军在台湾频繁进行军事演习，加大了对台湾的压力。 在台北和华盛顿的反应中，印度尼西亚海军表示，其与中国海军的活动“本质上不是战斗活动”，并且“无意进行战斗训练”。 台湾淡江大学国际事务与战略研究所副教授林英宇告诉德国之声，中国与印尼的演习没有什么战术意义。 他说：“这不像联合海上演习那么实际，但中国希望宣示其在该海域的能力。” 不过，日本国际问题研究所研究台印尼关系的客座研究员拉蒂·卡比纳瓦(Ratih Kabinawa)告诉德国之声，无论演习的意义如何，印尼都应该预料到台湾会做出一些反应。 “无论你喜欢与否，印度尼西亚现在都被拖入了这种地缘政治游戏，”她说。 卡比纳瓦补充说，此次演习是中国迄今为止用来证明其恐吓台湾合理性的最低级别的海军活动之一。 她说：“印度尼西亚在这方面也必须保持谨慎。”她补充说，雅加达应该“不要太天真”，认为参加与中国的“定期演习”不会引起人们的担忧……

reflection.en: In a world of complex geopolitical dynamics, nations often strive to maintain peace and neutrality. Indonesia's efforts to navigate its foreign policy amidst regional tensions reflect the ongoing challenge of living at peace with all, as far as it depends on them. This pursuit requires wisdom and a steadfast commitment to de-escalation and understanding.
reflection.zh: 在复杂的地缘政治格局中，各国常努力维持和平与中立。印度尼西亚在区域紧张局势中努力调整其外交政策，反映了在力所能及的范围内与所有人和平相处的持续挑战。这种追求需要智慧和对缓和局势、增进理解的坚定承诺。

verse.textEn: If it is possible, as far as it depends on you, live at peace with everyone.
verse.textZh: 若是能行，总要尽力与众人和睦。

title.en: One Nation MP admits the party's true migration target 'isn't too different' from Labor's

summary.en: Pauline Hanson has had to intervene after one MP's revised intake figure raised key questions.
summary.zh: 这是一则来自澳洲栏目的新闻，重点涉及对脆弱群体的怜悯。如需完整细节，请阅读英文原始报道。

body.en:
One Nation's immigration stance is under question after an MP said the party would include an extra 100,000 people annually in its policy — bringing its target total higher than present forecasts under Labor.

Farrer MP David Farley, who clinched Sussan Ley's old seat from the coalition at a by-election, told the ABC Insiders program on Sunday morning that his party had decided to separate a "true NOM", or net overseas migration figure, from certain other categories of migrants.

However, party leader Pauline Hanson was forced to quickly intervene, refuting the claims just hours later on social media. Party policy is to "cut net overseas migration to 130,000".

This contradicts messaging from Farley, who said One Nation's stated policy of getting net overseas migration down to 130,000 excluded people brought in under a Pacific scheme, aged-care nurses and other in-demand skilled workers.

Your trusted source for staying up-to-date with the world around you. Get free daily news updates and analysis, straight to your inbox.

Adding those groups would amount to an additional 100,000 arrivals, bringing the total to 230,000 — 5,000 more than the budget forecast of 225,000 in the coming four years.

"What we're doing is we're focusing on the NOM in its true form, and then we've got these programs that have been available now for over a decade that drive our economy," Farley told Insiders.

"The raw number is not too different, but the reality is, where do we need them?

"We don't need them in the great urban metroplex — we need them out to be productive, working in agriculture, engineering, mining."

The comments come as public debate continues around the optimum level of migration to Australia.

Net overseas migration dropped to 306,000 in 2024-25, brought down from a post-pandemic peak of 538,000 under Liberal-National government policy.

Cabinet minister Chris Bowen said net overseas migration could not just be redefined.

"My overwhelming conclusion was he's pretty comfortable with what the government's doing," Bowen told reporters.

"I'm not sure what campaign One Nation's going to run on migration if they're effectively backing in what the Albanese government is doing."

"These are not semantic distinctions. They have real consequences for housing, infrastructure, essential services, wages, jobs and the economy," he said.

Marathon organisers have acknowledged the "unfortunate error", with the medal showing the German stadium’s distinctive diamond-patterned exterior rather than the flatter design of Sydney’s Allianz Stadium.

"A little too much international flavour has found its way onto the back of the finishers' medal, with an incorrect depiction of the stadium," a Sydney Marathon spokesperson said.

"We're not going to run from it, it was an unfortunate error, though it's certainly given everyone something to talk about this weekend, mostly in good humour."

"Perhaps they tried to find something else they had in common: Allianz Arena — Sydney Opera — Unique Architecture — Both are worth a visit!"

The reverse side of the Sydney Marathon medal features a widely praised blue-and-gold design by Indigenous artist Ambrose Killian, who told the Agence-France Presse news agency that he was not involved in creating the Sydney skyline design.

"My artwork and creative contribution to this year's medal was specifically for the lanyard and the front side of the medal only," he said.

"I had no involvement in the design or production of the reverse side of the medal, including the incorrect inclusion of Allianz Arena in Munich, Germany, rather than Allianz Stadium in Sydney.

"I take my work very seriously and would like to reiterate that my artwork story, importance and originality remains."

title.en: First mammal infected with bird flu in Australia as 'devastating virus' spreads beyond birdlife

summary.en: Australia has reported its first mammal infection with bird flu, indicating the virus is spreading beyond avian populations. The agriculture minister acknowledged the situation as distressing but not unforeseen.

body.en:
Australia has recorded its first case of bird flu in a mammal, as the deadly virus continues to spread.

A long-nosed fur seal at Beachport in South Australia tested positive for H5 bird flu, authorities confirmed on Sunday.

It's the first confirmed case of the strain in a mammal in Australia and is believed to have been contracted from wild birds.

Agriculture Minister Julie Collins said the development was distressing but not unexpected.

"Although this is a concerning development, it is not unexpected for us to start to see infection in other wildlife, particularly in marine mammals, particularly in areas where there are high infection rates in wild birds," she said.

Your trusted source for staying up-to-date with the world around you. Get free daily news updates and analysis, straight to your inbox.

"Sadly, we also know that once the H5 bird flu is spreading in the natural environment, it is not possible to avoid significant losses."

Chief executive of the Invasive Species Council Jack Gough said overseas mammal-to-mammal transmission had resulted in high fatality rates.

"We know from South America and Antarctica that mammal-to-mammal transmission among seals quickly led to high mortality rates, particularly among pups," he said.

"We are still just at the early stages of this devastating virus and the bad news is going to keep coming for our wildlife as it spreads around the continent and between species."

This follows an increase in bird fatalities since the virus was first detected on Australia's shores in June.

South Australia has the highest number of confirmed cases, with 182 positive detections.

Victoria has recorded 86 cases, Western Australia 10, NSW 11, and Tasmania nine.

So far, no cases have been detected in an agricultural setting, and the health risk to humans remains low.

The public is urged to report sick-looking birds to authorities and not to approach or touch them.

Fire authorities across Australia are preparing for a spring fire season that could bring sharply different risks depending on the region, with some areas facing an early bushfire threat while others contend with delayed wet seasons and severe weather.

"I will just remind everyone that the bureau's long-range forecast does incorporate all of the influences from our surrounding oceans and the atmosphere as well as other long-term climate trends.

"I mention that because I'm sure most people are aware an El Niño event is underway, it is strengthening, and it is going to be a very strong one," Egan said.

title.en: They rejected the Aussie dream. What they bought instead cost $130,000

summary.zh: 这是一则来自澳洲栏目的新闻，重点涉及和平与克制。如需完整细节，请阅读英文原始报道。

body.en:
A sprawling property with a white picket fence was once a symbol of success, but for Lizzie Villestas this version of home ownership is a trap, not a triumph.

"For many, success is measured by the square footage of your property and for us, we began to see large homes as a different kind of trap; one that comes with massive debt and endless maintenance," Villestas told SBS Chinese.

For more than three years, she has lived in a tiny house measuring just eight metres long and 2.5 metres wide, or 20 square metres. The average floor area of a new house in Australia was 232.3 square metres in 2021/22, according to the Australian Bureau of Statistics.

Villestas' space may be small, but it's been thoughtfully designed, featuring a deep green and timber colour palette, akin to the surrounding bushland. It's even fitted with a study loft, bathtub and an indoor fireplace.

A labour of love, the property was constructed by Villestas and David Menhennett over 18 months and cost about $130,000. The couple now live in north-east Victoria and can relocate their tiny house on wheels across Australia, as desired.

Your trusted source for staying up-to-date with the world around you. Get free daily news updates and analysis, straight to your inbox.

"It was a virtual no-brainer ... most Australians are looking down the barrel of now ... a 30-year mortgage of up to a million dollars to own an average home," said Menhennett, who previously lived in Hong Kong for around 20 years.

Compounded by Australia's housing crisis , experts believe demand for tiny houses is surging. But while these properties promise big savings, they're often associated with regulatory red tape and financing complexities .

Driven by a desire to achieve financial freedom , Danielle Lester decided to adopt tiny house living two years ago.

She now serves as president of the volunteer-run Australian Tiny Homes Association (ATHA) but admits it's difficult to gather robust data about the number of tiny homes in Australia.

"Our membership base doesn't fully represent the amount of people who are living in tiny homes around Australia, and we find because of the regulatory complexity, a lot of people are choosing to do it under the radar, at their own risk," Lester told SBS News.

"Obviously, people have got no other option at the moment but to find a roof to put over their heads."

In part, that's because there's no official national definition for what constitutes a tiny house in Australia. Instead, they are regulated by federal, state and local government authorities — whose planning policies can often overlap and contradict each other.

Griffith University emeritus professor Paul Burton said tiny homes are also classified differently depending on their design.

body.en:

But since landing the role of medical student Victoria Javadi on HBO Max's The Pitt — a show that swept last year's awards season, taking home five Emmys and two Golden Globes — the 29-year-old Adelaidian has had a front-row seat to what being a rising star actually does to a person.

For Azeez, the experience has brought an expected lesson about success: even as her career takes off in Hollywood, home — and the ordinariness that comes with it — remains her way of keeping perspective.

"It's not that I'm famous or anything — thank God — but there is that kind of thing starting and happening in these small ways. It's bad for you."

"I think it's really good for your soul to get off the chessboard a little bit," she says.

It's a grounded way to talk about a career that, by any measure, is having a moment.

The Pitt turned Azeez into one of the more closely watched Australian acting newcomers in recent years — a stardom made stranger by the fact that she remained largely incognito at home even as the show became an international hit.

The series has since been renewed for a third season, giving Azeez another opportunity to build on the role that brought her to a global audience.

When she flew to Los Angeles to shoot the medical drama, she wasn't chasing a long-held plan, and she certainly wasn't arriving fresh out of drama school — she'd actually been rejected from one years earlier.

She got there through a mix of good luck and bad: a safer arts admin job after drama school rejection, then a boss who, sensing her heart wasn't in the work, booked her an audition for a short film without asking (thankfully, she landed it).

That opportunity pulled her into Adelaide's indie filmmaking scene, eventually leading to her feature debut in 2023's Birdeater and, after the film screened internationally, to US representation and an audition for The Pitt.

Growing up in Adelaide, the daughter of Indo-Fijian migrants, Azeez never really considered acting an option.

"The narrative was: do not become an actor, so help me, God," she says of her parents' position.

"It's not unreasonable for migrant parents — who've given up their culture and their home to give you financial stability, security and safety — it's not unreasonable for them to say, 'I gave up everything to give you safety. Please don't mess this up.'"

Even now, as her profile continues to rise, Azeez talks about the industry as if she's still waiting for her luck to run out.

body.en:
Lawyers for a third woman who allegedly endured sexual assault during a hotel gathering of Sydney Swans players say she is suffering an "incredibly traumatic experience".

Personal injury specialist Slater and Gordon has been engaged by one of now three women allegedly hired as adult entertainers to party with five Swans players at the Pullman Hotel in East Melbourne on Monday morning.

The firm has been asked to determine whether the woman "involved in the alleged sexual assaults" has grounds to file a civil claim, says senior lawyer Jackson Pannam.

''Everyone deserves to be safe going about their life, at home, at work and in public spaces without risk of being assaulted or harmed,'' he said in a statement on Saturday.

According to Mr Pannam, the woman, who contacted police immediately after the alleged assault, has had her world turned upside down and is navigating an "incredibly traumatic experience".

Two other women at the centre of an investigation involving the five players were subjected to "abhorrent" actions, the women's lawyer had alleged.

The Sydney Swans have "categorically confirmed" no members of the AFL club's staff were involved in police investigations into the alleged sexual assault at Melbourne's Pullman Hotel.

Five players - Isaac Heeney, Chad Warner, Nick Blakey, Riley Bice and James Jordon - have been suspended for the rest of the season for "breaching club standards".

The sanctions on the five men are separate to the police investigations into sexual assault allegations and the events at East Melbourne's Pullman Hotel in the early hours of Monday morning.

Victoria Police and Sydney released separate statements on Saturday, with the Swans repeating a previous statement that no club representatives other than the five suspended players were in the hotel room in question.

"The Sydney Swans supports the action taken by Victoria Police in releasing today's statement regarding the investigation," the Swans said in their statement.

"The Sydney Swans categorically confirms that no member of staff is involved in the investigation. This includes being in the hotel room central to the police investigation.

"The club reiterates that no player has been interviewed by police at this stage."

Victoria Police said their investigation was ongoing and no charges have been laid.
